title: How generative AI models work
learningObjective: Describe how generative AI models work: tokens, embeddings, attention, next-token prediction, the context window, sampling parameters, and why grounding matters.
foundation: A large language model (LLM) is trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next piece of text. Given 'The cat sat on the', it predicts 'mat' is likely.
Text is split into tokens: whole words or pieces of words, about 4 characters of English each. Models read and write tokens, and you pay per token.
To answer, the model calculates a probability for every possible next token, picks one, adds it, and repeats until it's done. That's why answers stream word by word.
Models aren't databases. They can produce fluent answers that are wrong ('hallucinations'). Grounding, which means giving the model your data in the prompt, makes answers more accurate.
engineer: Transformer architecture: tokens become embeddings (vectors that capture meaning); self-attention lets each token weigh every other token in the context; stacked layers produce a probability distribution over the vocabulary for the next token.

Training: pre-training on large text corpora learns language patterns; instruction tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback make chat models follow instructions and refuse unsafe requests. Fine-tuning adapts a model further with your examples.

Context window: the maximum tokens (system prompt + history + grounding data + the answer) in one request. Exceed it and older content must be dropped or summarised. Input and output tokens are both billed.

Sampling: temperature (higher = more random and creative; near 0 = most likely tokens, more consistent), top_p (sample only from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum to p), max_output_tokens (caps the answer; finish reason 'length' means it was cut off). Adjust temperature or top_p, not both. Some reasoning models don't accept these and use a reasoning-effort setting instead.
Multimodal generative models also accept or produce images and audio; image models generate pixels from text through diffusion or similar techniques.
Grounding / retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): retrieve relevant content (often with embeddings and vector search) and add it to the prompt so the model answers from it, with citations.

example.title: Why the FAQ bot varied its answers
body: A company FAQ bot gave different wording each time and once invented a refund rule. With temperature 1.0 it sampled less likely tokens; with no grounding it relied on training data.
The team set temperature to 0.2, added the refund policy to the prompt (grounding), and raised max_output_tokens because long answers were ending with finish reason 'length'.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Foundry portal > Playground > Parameters: temperature, top_p, max tokens.
Compare answers at temperature 0 and 1 for the same prompt.
Watch the token counts in the response details.
configuration.cli:
# Create a Foundry resource and project (billable only when used)
az group create --name rg-ai901 --location eastus2
az cognitiveservices account create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus2 --custom-domain contoso-ai --allow-project-management
az cognitiveservices account project create --name support --resource-group rg-ai901 --account-name contoso-ai
# Deploy a model (Global Standard, 50K TPM)
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --deployment-name chat-model --model-name gpt-5-mini --model-version <version> --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 50
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-ai901 -Location eastus2
New-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai -Type AIServices -SkuName S0 -Location eastus2 -CustomSubdomainName contoso-ai
# Projects and deployments: use the Foundry portal or Azure CLI
configuration.python:
response = openai.responses.create(
    model="chat-model",
    input="Suggest three names for a cat cafe.",
    temperature=1.0,        # more creative
    max_output_tokens=100,  # cap the answer length
)
print(response.output_text, response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens)

troubleshooting.fix: Raise the limit or ask for shorter answers.

troubleshooting.symptom: The model states false facts confidently.
troubleshooting.fix: Add retrieved data to the prompt and ask for citations.

comparisons.difference: A model generates text from patterns; search retrieves existing documents. RAG combines them.
Both control randomness: temperature reshapes probabilities; top_p truncates the candidate list.

misconceptions.myth: Models look up answers in a database.
misconceptions.reality: They predict tokens from learned patterns.
It makes them more consistent, not more truthful.
Tokens are often parts of words.

architectureDecisions: Use low temperature for factual tasks, higher for creative ones.
Ground answers in your data for accuracy.
Budget tokens: prompt size and answer length drive cost and latency.
